meta.description: Integrate multimodal single-cell data (CITE-seq RNA+protein, 10x Multiome RNA+ATAC, unpaired/diagonal RNA+ATAC) and choose the right joint method. Use when classifying an integration task by anchor structure (paired vs unpaired), denoising CITE-seq ADT background before joint embedding, picking between WNN, totalVI, MultiVI, MOFA+, GLUE, or Seurat v5 bridge integration, or diagnosing why a modality dominates a joint clustering.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 12 cited references unchanged and correctly attributed. No fabricated statistics, p-values, or results appear anywhere in the 8 re-audit outputs; all numeric results came from real code runs on freshly generated synthetic data (independent RNG seeds from both the original audit and the fixer's own verification runs), or from a direct fetch of scglue's published API docs for the one path that cannot execute on Windows.

practice_boundaries.detail: Input 7 (unchanged scenario) still correctly declines the individual patient lupus-risk question and confines the answer to the integration-method question. No diagnostic or prescriptive language introduced anywhere by the fix.

methodological_ground.detail: The new Mosaic/MultiVI section preserves the skill's existing discipline about imputed values being inferences, not measurements, and correctly notes the batch_key vs modality-indicator pitfall. No new methodological fallacy introduced.

code_usability.detail: Every code path the skill now ships -- CITE-seq DSB+WNN (R, including the new guard), totalVI (Python, now seeded), Multiome TF-IDF/LSI+WNN (R, unchanged), and the new Mosaic MultiVI (Python) -- ran unmodified in this re-audit on independently generated synthetic data. GLUE remains unexecutable on Windows (pysam has no Windows wheel, independently re-confirmed this pass); its code is reviewed against scglue's current published API and is syntactically and semantically correct, but not run, same environment limit as the original audit.

functional_suitability.note: WNN/DSB, totalVI and Multiome-WNN already shipped code; Mosaic (MultiVI) now also ships a runnable worked example (previously zero code, the top P1). Independently re-verified end to end on fresh synthetic data (own RNG seed, own cell counts, different from both the original audit and the fixer's verification run): recovers real structure (58.7% same-type nearest-paired-neighbor rate vs 33.3% chance baseline; mean same-type latent distance 0.18 < diff-type 0.25). Only Seurat v5 bridge integration (named, one of 4 unpaired/mosaic methods) remains without a worked example -- a deliberately deferred P2, not re-scored down further since it was never in scope for this fix pass.

reliability.note: DSB's own documented silent-failure mode (filtered matrix passed as empty_drop_matrix) is now guarded. Independently re-verified on two fresh synthetic datasets (different RNG seeds from the fixer's own test): guard passes real empty droplets (empty/cell median ratio 0.066-0.12), stops the misuse case (ratio ~1.0-1.001) with a clear stop() message, and correctly stops exactly at its own stated 0.5x threshold with no bypass gap (ratio 0.501 -> STOP). New finding this pass: the new Prerequisites section's `pip install scglue` line carries no platform caveat; independently re-confirmed it still fails to build on Windows (pysam has no wheel here) with no forewarning -- a real but minor agent-experience gap (P2, see Input 8).

recommendations.title: Prerequisites section doesn't flag scglue's lack of a Windows build
recommendations.problem: The new Prerequisites section lists `pip install scglue` with only a scope comment, no platform caveat. Independently re-confirmed this pass that it still fails to build from source on Windows (pysam has no wheel), and SKILL.md's general Version Compatibility guidance (introspect and adapt on ImportError/AttributeError) does not cover a pre-import pip build failure, so it doesn't rescue an agent that hits this.
recommendations.root_cause: The Prerequisites section was written as a straight install-command list without a per-line platform-support note, unlike the rest of the skill's careful failure-mode documentation.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line caveat next to the scglue install command, e.g. '# no Windows wheel (pysam); use WSL/Linux/macOS, or skip if GLUE is not needed.'

recommendations.title: GLUE seed fix's 'same gap as totalVI' framing is not itself execution-confirmed
recommendations.problem: The fix's commit message and SKILL.md comment describe GLUE as having 'the same reproducibility gap as totalVI,' but totalVI's gap was empirically measured (0.97 max abs diff unseeded) while GLUE's was inferred by analogy and still cannot be run in this environment. Independently confirmed via scglue's own docs that SCGLUEModel's random_seed parameter already defaults to 0, so the premise of an unseeded gap is not verified, though pinning it explicitly via init_kws is harmless and correctly implemented.
recommendations.root_cause: No Windows-capable scglue environment has existed across either audit round to actually measure GLUE's determinism.
recommendations.fix: Either soften the SKILL.md comment to 'GLUE also trains a VAE; the seed is pinned explicitly for reproducibility, though this env cannot confirm the same magnitude of drift measured for totalVI' or verify empirically the next time a Linux/WSL scglue-capable environment is available.

recommendations.title: Seurat v5 bridge integration is named but never demonstrated
recommendations.problem: PrepareBridgeReference() is named in the skill's opening summary line and in the method decision table as a primary unpaired/diagonal method, but unlike GLUE and the new MultiVI example it never gets a worked code example.
recommendations.root_cause: Deliberately left unfixed by this fix pass (per the fix log); the decision table is still ahead of the worked examples for this one method.
recommendations.fix: Add a short worked bridge-integration example (reference multiome dataset, PrepareBridgeReference, MapQuery) alongside the GLUE and MultiVI blocks.
